title: An integral basis gives a rational continuous matrix
statement: Let K be a topological field, A a subring, L a sheaf of K_X-modules, e:L|U ≅ K_U^n, and P an integral lattice pair on V → U [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-pair-image-classification]. Fix finite local generators q of P.module which are bases. For a basis member q.X(i) and any arrow W → V factoring through it, there is G ∈ GL_n(C(|W|,K)) whose restriction to every T → W gives exactly e(P.image(T)) as its integral column span [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-section-matrix].

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; An integral basis gives a rational continuous matrix

proof.text: Restrict the specified integral basis to W. Tensor the finite free integral module with K, identifying the sheafified tensor product with the free rational module by the basis formula. Compose with P.rationalization and e to get mutually inverse coordinate maps.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; An integral basis gives a rational continuous matrix

proof.text: If W is nonempty, evaluate at a point; invariant basis number over K gives the equality of the two finite ranks. Reindex the integral basis by Fin n. Its rational coordinates and the coordinates of the inverse form G and G⁻¹. Every integral section is an integral linear combination of these columns, and naturality gives the same formula on all T → W. If W is empty all coefficient and free section modules on its slice are singletons, and both nonempty images are the whole singleton. Rank zero is the same finite free computation.
